explanations.explanation: That's the one, baker. They swear by the LORD's name and invoke the God of Israel, "but not in truth or righteousness" (Isaiah 48:1). Saying the right words is the easy part. The LORD is looking at what's behind them, and He says it's missing.

Good guess, friend, but this verse never mentions sacrifices or offerings. The LORD says they swear by His name and invoke the God of Israel, "but not in truth or righteousness" (Isaiah 48:1). Their words were there. The truth and righteousness behind them weren't.

Close, baker, because the verse does say they invoke the God of Israel. But the thing missing isn't songs or prayers. The LORD says they do it "but not in truth or righteousness" (Isaiah 48:1). The words were showing up. The truth wasn't.
That's it, friend. The LORD says, "Suddenly I acted, and they came to pass" (Isaiah 48:3). He said it first, and then it happened. No long wait, no maybe.
Not this time, baker. The LORD never says they were forgotten. He says, "Suddenly I acted, and they came to pass" (Isaiah 48:3). They happened, and they happened fast.
Nice try, friend, but nothing in the verse says they were changed. The LORD says, "Suddenly I acted, and they came to pass" (Isaiah 48:3). What He foretold is what came to pass.

Yes, baker. The LORD says, "For I knew that you are stubborn; your neck is iron and your forehead is bronze" (Isaiah 48:4). Then He says, "Therefore I declared it to you long ago" (Isaiah 48:5). So the early warning came with that knowledge behind it.

Not fearful, friend. The word the LORD uses is "stubborn," and He backs it up with iron and bronze: "your neck is iron and your forehead is bronze" (Isaiah 48:4). Nobody describes a scaredy-cat with metal. That's a hard head.

Good try, baker, but "weary" isn't the word here. The LORD says, "For I knew that you are stubborn; your neck is iron and your forehead is bronze" (Isaiah 48:4). Tired people drag their feet. Stubborn people plant them.

Careful, friend, it's the other way around. The LORD announced it ahead of time "so that you could not claim, 'My idol has done this; my carved image and molten god has ordained it'" (Isaiah 48:5). He took away that excuse before they could even use it.

Right, baker. The LORD declared it long ago "so that you could not claim, 'My idol has done this; my carved image and molten god has ordained it'" (Isaiah 48:5). He wasn't handing them an excuse. He was shutting the door on one.
You got it, baker. The LORD says, "From now on I will tell you of new things, hidden things unknown to you" (Isaiah 48:6). The old things already happened. Now He's got something fresh to say.

Fair guess, friend, but those words aren't in this verse. The LORD says, "From now on I will tell you of new things, hidden things unknown to you" (Isaiah 48:6). That's new things, and they're hidden ones.

That one's not here, baker. The LORD says, "From now on I will tell you of new things, hidden things unknown to you" (Isaiah 48:6). He's talking about what He'll announce next, and it's new and hidden.
Close, friend, but the LORD says the opposite. About these new things He says, "you have not heard of them before today" (Isaiah 48:7). They're brand new to His people.
That's right, baker. The LORD says, "They are created now, and not long ago; you have not heard of them before today" (Isaiah 48:7). First time hearing it, so nobody gets to say they saw it coming.
Not quite, friend. The LORD says, "for a long time your ears have not been open" (Isaiah 48:8). So it's closed ears, and for a long stretch.
Yes, baker. The LORD says, "You have never heard; you have never understood; for a long time your ears have not been open" (Isaiah 48:8). Those ears had been shut a good while.

explanations.answer: For the sake of His name
explanations.explanation: That's the one, friend. The LORD says, "For the sake of My name I will delay My wrath" (Isaiah 48:9). He gives the reason Himself, and it's about His name.

explanations.answer: For the sake of their prayers
explanations.explanation: Good thought, baker, but the LORD doesn't say that. He says, "For the sake of My name I will delay My wrath; for the sake of My praise I will restrain it" (Isaiah 48:9). The reason He gives is His own name.

explanations.answer: For the sake of their fathers
explanations.explanation: Not this time, friend. The verse never mentions their fathers. The LORD says, "For the sake of My name I will delay My wrath" (Isaiah 48:9). His name is the reason He gives.
Yes, baker. The LORD says, "for the sake of My praise I will restrain it, so that you will not be cut off" (Isaiah 48:9). He holds His wrath back, and He says that's so they won't be cut off.

Actually, friend, that one's true. The LORD says, "for the sake of My praise I will restrain it, so that you will not be cut off" (Isaiah 48:9). He restrains His wrath, and He names not being cut off as the purpose.
Right, baker. The LORD says, "I have tested you in the furnace of affliction" (Isaiah 48:10). A furnace, and not a gentle one.

explanations.answer: In the depths of the sea
explanations.explanation: Not the sea, friend. The LORD says, "I have tested you in the furnace of affliction" (Isaiah 48:10). Fire is what this verse is about, not water.

explanations.answer: In the belly of the fish
explanations.explanation: Ha, that's a different book, baker. That's Jonah, the prophet who ended up inside a great fish (Jonah 1:17). Here the LORD says, "I have tested you in the furnace of affliction" (Isaiah 48:10).
Other way around, friend. The LORD says, "I will not yield My glory to another" (Isaiah 48:11). His glory stays His.
That's right, baker. The LORD says, "For how can I let Myself be defamed? I will not yield My glory to another" (Isaiah 48:11). He won't hand it over to anyone else.
